Where the tendrils make contact, the brick material appears to be actively eroding and spalling, causing larger chunks of the structure to shear and break away in a constant process of decay. The overall image is defined by deep texture, crumbling mortar, and the expanding patterns of natural intrusion.

The composition shows a realistic brick structure with detailed mortar lines and natural texture variations. Root systems emerge from the bottom of the canvas, growing upward through the mortar joints with organic, sinuous paths. As they progress, these roots cause visible stress fractures in the brick faces and trigger spalling effects where chunks break away from contact points. The scene evolves slowly over time, creating a sense of continuous decay and natural intrusion. The visual effect emphasizes the contrast between the rigid, aged brick structure and the fluid, destructive force of the roots pushing through it.
